To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CT105 is toxic to Xenopus laevis oocytes, and the toxic effect of the peptide is dependent on Na+ influx and on intracellular events.
the toxic effect of the β- amyloid precursor protein (APP) C-terminus fragment is dependent on the Na+ concentration gradients.
CT105 toxicity in oocytes is dependent on Na+ influx and that the toxicity of CT105 to oocytes is mediated by intracellular events.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanism of action of the toxic C-terminal fragment of βAPP.
the role of Na+ and/or Ca2+ influx in the toxic effect of CT105.
understanding the molecular mechanisms of CT105-induced toxicity and how these relate to Aβ toxicity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the toxic effect of CT105 is due to a combination of Na+ influx and the intracellular Ca2+ increase, which is a result of a Ca2+ influx.
the CT105-induced toxic effect in oocytes is due to the combined effects of the Na+ and Ca+2 gradients.
intracellular events and Na+ influx are responsible for the observed toxic effects of CT105.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CT105-induced toxicity is mainly due to intracellular events, but that Na+ influx is also involved in the mode of operation of this peptide fragment.
CT105-induced toxicity is mediated by a Na+-dependent mechanism, involving Na+/Ca2+-exchanger and Na+/H+-exchanger.
CT105 toxicity is mainly mediated by the trans-membranous Na+ gradient and the resulting Ca2+ influx.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CT105-induced toxicity is dependent on Na+ influx.
the toxic effect of the β-APP C-terminal fragment is not due to the Aβ sequence, but to the C-terminal region of β-APP.
CT105-induced toxicity is dependent on the transmembrane Na+ concentration gradient.
